transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the final review for the 'Tidal Memory' installation in Gallery 4, scheduled October 12 through 15. The current draft plan proposes online-connected playback, eight visitor stations, 15-minute sessions, and a 5:00 PM public opening on October 12. Before I can approve this, I need to hear from each of you — rights, technical, accessibility, and artist representatives — on whether you have any conditions that must be added to this plan. Let's go around the room.

transcript.text: I need to flag several conditions from the music license. I reviewed the countersigned license this morning — it arrived after the exhibition packet was circulated, so the packet hasn't been updated yet. The license imposes three conditions: (1) Tidal Memory may be exhibited only through offline local playback — the current draft plan's online-connected playback would violate the license; (2) visitors may not photograph or record the installation; and (3) the exact credit line 'Music licensed from Harborlight Editions' must be used.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical condition. After yesterday's installation rehearsal, I completed the headset and network test and found that the approved headset model supports only six simultaneous stations — not eight as currently proposed. Additionally, each session must be limited to exactly 12 minutes to prevent thermal shutdown, not the 15-minute sessions in the current draft. The test report is still in the equipment vendor's queue, so this hasn't been circulated yet.

transcript.text: I need to flag accessibility conditions. I confirmed with the festival's access consultant today that one of the six stations must be a seated, step-free station, and that every visitor notice must display the exact warning 'Flashing light and sudden sound'. The consultant's written confirmation was received after the draft visitor signage was already sent to print, so the signage will need to be reprinted with the corrected warning.
